definition: The copyright in the song itself, its melody and words, usually owned by a music publisher. Also called publishing.
The copyright in one specific recording of a song, usually owned by a label.
Permission from a music publisher to use a composition in a game or film.
Permission from a label to use a specific recording.
How long a license lasts. Reported game cases run from seven to 10 years.
The countries a license covers; worldwide costs more than a limited set.
Which uses a license covers, such as in-game playback per platform, trailers or store pages.
A flat one-time fee with no ongoing royalties.
A license with no end date. It costs more and is described as rare in games.
A pre-agreed right to extend a license to sequels, DLC or ports.
Anyone who owns a share of a song or recording; one track can have six or more.
Pulling a game from digital sale, often because its licenses have expired.
Units shipped to retailers plus digital sales, as Take-Two reports them; not the same as copies bought by players.
A small, fast patch. GTA V's 2026 Moloko removal arrived in one.
